title: Mughal Miniature Painting

endcard.line: Pictures: Kesav Das and Mah Muhammad (CC0); unknown artist (The Met) (CC0); Ustad Mansur (CC0)

items.text: Humayun returns with two Persian painters
era of big illustrated histories ends

segments.say: When the emperor Humayun came back to India from exile in Persia, he brought two Persian painters with him, Abd al-Samad and Mir Sayyid Ali. A new style began.
Under Akbar, an imperial workshop of artists worked together. Their Hamzanama, a book of adventure tales, had about fourteen hundred paintings on large cotton pages.
It kept Persian habits, like richly decorated borders and a high viewpoint, but took far more interest in realistic portraits.
Akbar's own history, the Akbarnama, was painted in many versions, full of hunts, battles and court scenes.
Painters also made close studies of animals, birds and flowers, like these by Ustad Mansur.

anim.title: How it spread
items: The ruler's portrait becomes a leading subject
Muslim and Hindu princely courts take it up

segments.say: Under Jahangir and Shah Jahan, the royal portrait became a leading subject, and the style spread to Muslim and Hindu princely courts across India.
For GS One, link Mughal painting to Humayun's two Persian masters, Akbar's workshop, and the portraits and nature studies that followed.

sources: Wikipedia, 'Mughal painting' (read): originated from Persian miniature; Humayun, in exile at the Safavid court, returned to India with Persian artists Abd al-Samad and Mir Sayyid Ali; great period under Akbar, Jahangir and Shah Jahan; Akbar's imperial workshop; the Hamzanama on large pages of cotton with some 1400 miniatures; the Akbarnama produced in many versions; era of large illustrated imperial biographies ended around 1650; Persian decorated borders and elevated viewpoint continued; greater interest in realistic portraiture; realistic studies of animals and plants; the ruler's portrait spread to Muslim and Hindu princely courts

The Metropolitan Museum of Art collection records (via Wikimedia Commons) for the three folios shown: Hamzanama folio, Akbarnama folio 'Akbar Hunting', and 'Diving Dipper and Other Birds' attributed to Ustad Mansur, Shah Jahan Album

quiz.q: Which two Persian painters came to India with Humayun?
options: Abd al-Samad and Mir Sayyid Ali
quiz.why: Humayun brought Abd al-Samad and Mir Sayyid Ali back from Persia.

options: about 1,400 paintings on large cotton pages
quiz.why: Some 1400 miniatures on unusually large cotton pages.

quiz.q: What was new in Mughal painting compared to Persian miniatures?
quiz.why: Borders and viewpoint came from Persia; realistic portraiture was the Mughal turn.
